writer_0xe0.+0xc8: checksum_generator_ (FileChecksumGenerator*, 8) -- NOT read (UpdateFileChecksum is the member that uses it)
writer_0xe0.+0xd1: perform_data_verification_ (bool, 1) -- READ: gates the per-chunk checksum arm (pinned difference from WriteBufferedWithChecksum, which never consults it)
writer_0xe0.+0xd4: buffered_data_crc32c_checksum_ (uint32, 4) -- NOT read here (the fresh per-chunk Extend replaces the handoff; pinned difference from WriteBufferedWithChecksum)

observations: The CPU half of the timer guard is DEAD in this FDE: the flag byte at -0x18f is written 0 at 0x605012c and never set, the second clock slot at -0x170 is never filled, and no clock-or-default helper is called, so the slot-22 stop at 0x605071b is unreachable and the stop always takes the NowNanos branch (0x6050af8). The model records wd_cpu_nanos = 0 at every perf level, and the bindings group pins timer_guard_cpu_armed = False for perf levels 0..5. This is a pinned difference from both siblings, whose CPU halves are armed iff perf_level > 3.

file_advance and leftover_tail are computed LAZILY at the success epilogue (0x6050803..0x605081a) from the saved entry cursize_ (-0x218) and alignment (-0x220), not up front: the pad step only rounds cursize_ up, and the loop writes the whole padded buffer. The failure path restores cursize_ from the same two saved values (file_advance + leftover_tail = entry cursize_).

Three TEST_SYNC_POINT gates fire PER CHUNK (0x6050108 loop-head, 0x6050795 success-tail, 0x60507bd bytes-add), all through the helper 0x606d9f0 when the sync-point global *0x64ed5d0 is non-null. The bytes-add gate fires only when the IOStats-bytes flag is clear -- it sits between the flag check and the bytes add. The string names are not asserted; the model records the site addresses. The binary runs the tail sync point BEFORE the IOSTATS_ADD(bytes_written) while upstream lists the bytes add first -- same observable behaviour, a scheduling difference.

The checksum is a FRESH per-chunk computation, not a handoff: the binary calls the 19-byte crc32c::Extend helper (0x604c7e0) with (0, src, size) for every chunk when perform_data_verification_ is set, and never reads buffered_data_crc32c_checksum_ or buffered_data_with_checksum_. The live check pins this (the positioned_append events carry Value(b'hello'), Value(b' world') and Value(501 zero bytes), never the buffered 0x12345678). This is the pinned difference from WriteBufferedWithChecksum (handoff, always) and from WriteDirectWithChecksum (which recomputes the buffered value, per its oracle note).

There is NO PositionedAppend on the entry-empty path: cursize 0 skips the loop entirely (je 0x6050b06) and returns OK with file_advance = 0, leftover = 0, no file write, no flushed_size_ advance and no refit. The live check pins this (empty_buffer_no_write). QUIRK, recorded not hidden: on that path the sret subcode byte is read from -0x1d2, which no instruction on that path writes -- a stale stack slot; the model emits 0. The path is unreachable from Flush, which only calls WriteDirect with cursize_ > 0.

WriteDirect makes NO GetFileSize call and does NO perf_level save/restore -- both pinned differences from WriteBufferedWithChecksum, which calls GetFileSize once (return discarded) and saves/restores the TLS perf_level byte around the Append. filesize_ is never read or written here.

The failure event's type 9 IS FileOperationType::kPositionedAppend -- resolved by the live v8.1.1 read (include/rocksdb/listener.h:236-248, implicit 0-based: kRead 0, kWrite 1, kTruncate 2, kClose 3, kFlush 4, kSync 5, kFsync 6, kRangeSync 7, kAppend 8, kPositionedAppend 9, kOpen 10), matching upstream NotifyOnIOError(s, kPositionedAppend, file_name(), size, write_offset) in WriteDirect (lines 1576-1580). It follows the sibling pattern exactly: Flush's failure event carries its own op (4 = kFlush) and RangeSync's carries 7 = kRangeSync. The two trailing u64 fields are ordered (size, write_offset) -- the values passed to upstream NotifyOnIOError(s, kPositionedAppend, file_name(), size, write_offset). The model emits 9 exactly as observed. PINNED DIFFERENCE from WriteBufferedWithChecksum, whose failure event trails (left, old_size) with type 8.

The failure return restores cursize_ to the ENTRY value (buf_.Size(file_advance + leftover_tail)) and sets seen_error_ AFTER the listener notifications (0x6050693..0x60506a5), while WriteBufferedWithChecksum clears buf_ and resets the checksum after the events and WriteBuffered clears immediately after the failed Append, before the events -- a pinned ordering difference between the three siblings. The nanos guard stops after the sret build on the failure path (0x6050704..0x6050759), so a failed call's nanos elapsed time is still recorded but its bytes are never added to the IOStats counter.

The 0x61cf610 helper is a two-argument deep copy: the call sites set rdi = &dst (a stack slot) and rsi = src, and read the copy back from the slot after the call. The vendor census labels it Status::CopyState (one-arg signature), which does not match the observed calling convention; the name is recorded as an open unknown and the behaviour (deep copy, store at *dst) is what the model pins.

The 16-byte IOStatus copy drops byte 2 on every return path: the working status is copied as bytes 0-1, 3-4, 5, 8-15 with byte 2 forced to 0 (the code bytes spill at -0x1d1..-0x1d5, the high bytes of the low qword in reverse order, byte 2 never stored). The same shape holds in the siblings; the model reproduces it via Status.out_bytes().

WriteDirect itself has no census record, while its .cold does -- the same split as Flush (#6057), Append (#6041) and WriteBufferedWithChecksum (#6094), whose mains are also body-hash-only. The packet binds the main by its recomputed body hash and the .cold by the census record (13 relocations).

The only caller in the whole .text is Flush (0x6051a20 at 0x60520b9) -- WriteDirect is Flush's direct-I/O write step, reached only when pending_sync_ is set. No other member calls it; Append's verification arms call WriteBufferedWithChecksum, not WriteDirect.
unknowns: The TLS flag byte at fs-0x3f8+0x98 gating the IOStats bytes counter (+0x8) add: its identity is open. Modelled as iostats_bytes_flag (default clear = count).
The 0x61cf610 helper's symbol: the census labels it Status::CopyState (one arg) but the call sites pass (dst, src). Recorded as an open unknown; the deep-copy behaviour is pinned.

The TEST_SYNC_POINT string names in WriteDirect: the binary's literals are stripped (verified absent from the node #115 binary), so no per-site name is pinned from the binary. Upstream v8.1.1 names the loop's TEST_SYNC_POINT 'WritableFileWriter::Flush:BeforeAppend'; the binary calls the sync-point helper 0x606d9f0 from three sites (0x6050108, 0x6050795, 0x60507bd). The model records the three site addresses.

The bool at this+0xd9, read into the finish event: it is not named by the Append packet's writer layout and no upstream header in the 2019 mirror has a member at that offset. Modelled as flag_d9 and listed here as an open unknown (shared with the Flush packet).

The stale subcode byte on the entry-empty path: the sret subcode is read from -0x1d2, which no instruction on that path writes. The model emits 0; the actual byte in a live run would be whatever the stack slot held. The path is unreachable from Flush (cursize_ > 0), so the byte is unobservable through the only caller.

Flush, Append, WriteBuffered, WriteBufferedWithChecksum, WriteDirectWithChecksum and the RangeSync member are taken as oracles here (their bodies are separate FDEs; only WriteDirect.cold is census-bound in this packet). Their internal steps are modelled from the #6057/#6041/#6088/#6094 contracts and upstream source, not from their own binary bodies in this packet; WriteDirectWithChecksum is the natural follow-up.
